decisions.reason: As a visible product line on its own page that builds directly on the firm’s core geospatial integration offer, management is likely to keep backing it and explain any weak early uptake as normal market development.

The building data digital twin service fits the firm’s announced direction toward integrated, emerging geospatial solutions, so management would tend to persist with it despite only limited public visibility so far.

Although less central than core geospatial tools and only mentioned briefly on the website, the firm is still likely to retain this identity-related service because it supports enterprise integration and prior development effort invites continuation.

An open GIS application development framework is close to the firm’s technical core and strategic positioning, and as a multi-model line it likely reflects enough investment and commitment to make withdrawal unlikely.

This GIS-specific identity and access service is strategically complementary to the firm’s broader platform integration ambitions, so management would more likely continue than exit while attributing any slow adoption to customer implementation cycles.
